# TRW Idea Briefs, week of 13 Oct 2026 (Phase 2 run on 10 Oct 2026)
*Generated by Phase 2 from this cycle's ranked winners. Ed reviews, then Phase 3 renders. Reels are now in scope (Ed, 10 Oct 2026).*

**Run facts.** 11 watchlist accounts, 8 posts each, 36 posts inside the 60-day window. Six accounts are dormant (no post in 90 days). This is the first run since 24 June.

---

## What's winning, last 60 days

| # | Pattern | Example and numbers | Why it worked | TRW fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mechanic answers a question people argue about | @thecarcarenut "Should you pre-fill your oil filter?" 20.7K views, 106 comments; "Are old cars safer than newer cars?" 18.5K views in one day; "Low mileage cars aren't always as good as they seem" 10K views | A question with two camps. People comment to disagree, and comments push reach | High. This is the honest-mechanic position in Reel form |
| 2 | Emergency how-to | @chrisfixit "stranded with a coolant leak, here's how to get home" 233K views | Fear plus a save-worthy answer. People save it for later | High. SG version: overheating on the expressway, dead battery in an HDB carpark, warning light on the way to work |
| 3 | Symptom, named, then the fix | @chrisfixit "how to stop your car smoking on startup" 25K likes | Specific symptom in the hook; the viewer self-selects | High. Carousel or Reel |
| 4 | Owner identity story | @koocester "What's a car that reflects you perfectly? For Ping, it's this Defender 110" 49K views in two days | Human story, SG person, their car. Identity plus social proof | Medium. TRW customers and their cars, with permission |
| 5 | Price transparency | @dow.detailing "$888 ceramic package covering:" plus the list | Shows the whole bill up front | High. What the $180 PPI covers; what a servicing tier includes |
| 6 | Process POV | @dow.detailing "doorstep pickup, full wash, delivered back" 392 views | Small numbers, but the pickup-to-return structure reads as care | Medium. Fits TRW's towing and collection |
| 7 | Curiosity about an old car | @koocesterautos "This 76-year-old Land Rover still runs?" | Age plus surprise | Low to medium. COE-renewal angle: "this 10-year-old car renewed its COE, here's what it needed" |

**Dropped.** The epoxy floor video (1.8M views, not our niche), the meme and prank posts, the Sentosa car meet, the Ferrari meet-and-greet. Entertainment and vanity reach, not bookings.

**The SG gap.** The accounts winning on mechanic content are two American talking-head mechanics. The Singapore accounts on the list are detailers, car media and car culture. I checked five SG workshops named in 2026 "best workshop" articles: kgcworkshop has 538 posts and 1,254 followers, dmotorwerkz has 312 posts and 224 followers, and Lee Sheng Auto (Kaki Bukit), Gold Autoworks and Precise Auto Service have between 0 and 5 posts. No SG workshop is doing pattern 1, 2 or 3 on Instagram. TRW already has 254 posts out; adding Reels in those three patterns puts it in an empty lane.

## Five angles for TRW (prompt 2 output)

1. **The question you argue about.** A mechanic gives a straight answer on something SG drivers disagree on: oil change interval in SG heat, premium versus regular petrol, idling to warm up, aircon on or off before switching off, whether low mileage is good news on an old car.
2. **Stranded in Singapore.** One emergency per post, what to do in order: temperature needle climbing on the PIE, battery dead in a carpark, a warning light on the way to work, a puncture on the AYE, driving through a flooded road.
3. **The symptom, named.** The exact thing the driver notices, the likely causes from cheap to dear, and the one check we do first. Aircon cold then warm, a squeal that stops when braking, a judder at 60, a smell after a drive.
4. **The honest cost sheet.** What the $180 pre-purchase inspection covers, what a COE-renewal check includes, the three bills after 100,000 km, with real figures.
5. **How we work.** The credibility set: the parts tray, the photo before we replace anything over the agreed amount, the drop-off walk-around, the 3 pm call when a job grows, moving day.

## Five opening lines (prompt 4 output, drafts; verify every technical claim before filming)

1. "Low mileage on a ten-year-old car. Not always the good news it looks like." (contrarian, mirrors this cycle's winner, localised to COE-age cars)
2. "Temperature needle climbing on the PIE. The first thing to do is not what most drivers do." (fear plus curiosity)
3. "The part we took out of your car is in this tray. It stays there until you've seen it." (specificity, trust)
4. "A clean pre-purchase report still saved this buyer money." (curiosity, save-value)
5. "Cold for five minutes, then warm. Could be a leaking condenser, not low gas." (symptom named, the "could be" hedge TRW actually uses, invites the comments)

## The week: 3 carousels, 2 Reels (experimental slots)

Mode rotation: Reel, H, E, Reel, B. Lanes: 1 myth-bust, 1 emergency, 1 cost sheet, 2 credibility.

## MON · Reel · Low mileage isn't always good news (myth-bust)
- **Source:** @thecarcarenut, 10K views in 4 days on the same claim, overseas.
- **Pattern borrowed:** mechanic answers the question people argue about.
- **TRW topic:** why a 10-year-old car with 60,000 km can need more than a 120,000 km car driven daily (short trips, seals and rubber age, batteries that sat).
- **Format:** Reel. Best version: Path C, you or a mechanic at the bench, 45 to 60 seconds, one take, auto captions, opening with the customer's belief ("low mileage means a good car, right?") and turning on it. This week's fallback: Path B, 15 to 25 seconds of real workshop photos with captions and one voiceover line.
- **Hook (first 2 seconds, on screen and spoken):** "Low mileage on a ten-year-old car. Not always the good news it looks like."
- **Beats:** hook; the two things that age by time not distance; the one thing we check first on a low-mileage car; soft close.
- **Business CTA:** "Send us the listing before you pay a deposit."
- **Why it works for us:** the exact claim that won this cycle, in the lane no SG workshop occupies, ending in a message that starts a PPI conversation.

## TUE · H Diagram · Temperature needle climbing on the expressway (emergency)
- **Source:** @chrisfixit coolant-leak rescue, 233K views.
- **Pattern borrowed:** emergency how-to, steps in order.
- **TRW topic:** the first five minutes when the needle climbs on the PIE, in the order that protects the engine.
- **Mode:** H Diagram (dashboard gauge called out, numbered steps).
- **Hook:** "Temperature needle climbing on the PIE. The first thing to do is not what most drivers do."
- **Slides:** cover; step 1 pull off safely and switch off; step 2 what to do with the aircon and heater and why; step 3 never open the cap; step 4 what to look for under the car; step 5 when to call a tow; CTA.
- **Business CTA:** "Keep this one. Our tow line is 24/7." (number on the slide; the profile says ration "Save this", it's in 30 of 70 captions)
- **Why it works for us:** every SG driver has watched that needle; the save is the ask, and the tow line is a revenue door.
- **Check before build:** Ed or a mechanic confirms the step order and wording.

## WED · E Spec Sheet · What the $180 pre-purchase inspection actually checks (cost sheet + credibility)
- **Source:** @dow.detailing's "$888 package covering:" list, plus the June research gap (no SG workshop publishes this).
- **Pattern borrowed:** price transparency as a full list.
- **TRW topic:** the 120-point check grouped into the five things a buyer cares about: accident history, engine and gearbox, suspension and brakes, electrical, road test. What a clean report is good for.
- **Mode:** E Spec Sheet.
- **Hook:** "What a $180 pre-purchase inspection actually looks at."
- **Slides:** cover; the five groups; what "clean" means; the negotiating line; CTA.
- **Business CTA:** "Book before you pay the deposit."
- **Why it works for us:** PPI has never been posted on the feed (0 of 238 captions mention it), the price is already public, and the post is a pure save.

## THU · Reel · The parts tray (credibility)
- **Source:** the credibility set from the 10 Oct research; no competitor version.
- **Pattern borrowed:** process POV (pattern 6), shrunk to one object.
- **TRW topic:** every part we take out stays in a tray until the customer has seen it, and why.
- **Format:** Reel, 15 to 20 seconds. Path A: one phone clip of the tray, hands placing a worn part next to the new one. Path B fallback: two photos.
- **Hook:** "The part we took out of your car is in this tray. It stays there until you've seen it."
- **Beats:** hook on the tray; why (you can see the wear yourself); the photo we send before anything over the agreed amount; close.
- **Business CTA:** "That's how a service here works. Book one."
- **Why it works for us:** it says "honest" without using the word, and it needs ten seconds of footage.

## FRI · B Cream Magazine · We're moving to Synergy @ KB (credibility, timing is Ed's call)
- **Source:** the move-day runbook (address switch 19 Oct). The runbook has Ed updating the Instagram bio on the day; a feed post is a separate decision.
- **TRW topic:** same team, new bay. New address, parking, lift, entrance, what doesn't change.
- **Mode:** B Cream Magazine (photo-led; needs 3 to 4 photos of the new bay).
- **Hook:** "Same team. New bay. Here's how to find us from the 19th."
- **Slides:** cover; the address and map; parking and entrance; what doesn't change; CTA.
- **Business CTA:** "Keep this for your next service."
- **Why it works for us:** the people who need it most are existing customers, and it pairs with the website and Google listing switch.
- **If the timing is wrong:** swap in A Editorial Dark, "The 3 pm call", what we say when a job grows mid-way and why we stop and ask first.

## Reel production notes

**Shape.** 9:16, hook on screen and spoken in the first 2 seconds, captions throughout (most viewers watch muted), no hashtag stack. Length follows the format: 45 to 90 seconds when someone talks to camera with one claim and a turn; 15 to 25 seconds for Path B photo Reels. Close on the verdict; the CTA lives in the caption.

**Path C, the one that actually wins (add to the filming hour):** you or a mechanic at the bench, phone on a stand, auto captions. Say the belief the customer holds, in their words ("low mileage means a good car, right?"), then turn on it, give two reasons, end on the verdict. One take, no cuts. Three of these in the filming hour covers three weeks of Reels.

**Path A shot list for Ed (one hour, phone, vertical, steady, no plates in frame):** car going up on the lift; old brake pad next to new; aircon gauge reading; the diagnostic laptop screen; a finger on a worn part; keys handed back; the new door at Synergy @ KB; tyre tread check with a coin; oil draining; a WhatsApp photo being sent to a customer. Add: the parts tray with a worn part placed in it.

**Path B (this week):** slow pan over real workshop photos from the library, captions, one voiceover line. Remotion assembles; Dom QAs; the scheduler posts.

**Plates.** The photo-sanitiser handles stills. Video needs a blur pass or framing that keeps plates out. Frame them out.

**First-3-seconds pacing of the three winning Reels (frame-by-frame pass, 10 Oct).**

| Reel | Length | Hook at 0:00 | First 3 seconds | Structure | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| @thecarcarenut, oil filter | 71 s | Spoken and captioned: "Do you need to pre-fill your oil filter?" | Locked-off talking head at a bench, 0 cuts, word-by-word captions. Problem named, not shown | Steelman the idea, turn at 0:15, two reasons, authority line, verdict | None. Ends on the verdict |
| @thecarcarenut, old cars safer | 103 s | He says the myth in the customer's voice ("old cars made with real steel are much safer"), caption "OLD CARS?" | Same bench, 0 cuts, hands tap the bench to act "solid steel" | "That is a very dangerous myth" at 0:08, hammer-versus-sponge analogy acted with hands, crumple-zone payoff, verdict, family close | None |
| @chrisfixit, coolant leak | 163 s | "Today I got really lucky," with the coolant puddle in shot from frame one | Handheld phone, one continuous tilt-up, 0 cuts, no captions. Problem shown before it's named | Leak close-up, stakes and promise, tape fix, refill, proof at running temperature, method 2, "do not drive on this" | None, but "get to your closest mechanic" twice |

What all three share: they open on the customer's own question or fault inside 2 seconds (no intro, no music beat, no title card); one person, one location, zero cuts in the hook; nobody asks for a follow or a like, the argument itself drives the comments; and they run long and hold the viewer with structure (claim, turn, reasons, verdict; or problem, promise, demo, proof), not with cuts.

The most copyable move: say the belief the customer already holds, in their words, then turn on it. It needs a phone on a stand, the bench, and auto captions. Nothing else.

What this changes for us: the 15-to-25-second rule from the Instagram post is not what wins in this niche. If you or a mechanic will talk to camera, 45 to 90 seconds with one claim and a clear turn beats a short cut-heavy clip. Path B photo Reels stay short (15 to 25 s) because photos can't hold longer. The business CTA goes in the caption, soft, not in the video.
